- Model consistently overestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast window, particularly when true values show upward momentum.
- Overreacts to recent high prices, producing exaggerated peaks that are not sustained — model overshoots after spikes.
- Tends to underestimate the mean-reversion effect, especially in the middle of the forecast window.
- Shows persistent lag in capturing the true trend direction — often delays turning points by 1–3 days.
- When the true price rises sharply, model fails to anticipate the full magnitude of the spike, underestimating the peak.
- In low-volatility periods, model tends to underestimate the true price, especially near the end of the forecast window.
- Model exhibits bias toward higher values when the historical mean is above 68.0, and lower values when below 67.0 — adjust for context-dependent baseline.
